title: Remixing Special Education Practices with Artificial Intelligence: UDL, EBP, and HLPs
extended_summary:
This article addresses how special education teacher preparation can adapt to the rapid growth of generative AI tools, especially large language models, by integrating them into existing evidence-based practices (EBPs), high-leverage practices (HLPs), and Universal Design for Learning (UDL). Rather than reporting an empirical evaluation, the paper offers guidance on how educators can "remix" current instructional practices with AI so that AI complements, rather than replaces, established special education methods.

The authors discuss policy and implementation considerations for AI in K-12 education, including privacy, bias, transparency, and responsible use. They present examples of AI tools that could support UDL principles (for example, adjusting reading level, creating alternative representations, and supporting engagement), EBPs (such as social narratives, task analysis, and video modeling), and HLPs (such as feedback, lesson design, and formative assessment). The paper also includes example class activities for preservice special education teachers to practice using AI in these ways.

The population and context are preservice and practicing special educators in K-12 settings, with a strong emphasis on special education teacher preparation. The paper concludes that AI has substantial potential to enhance inclusive instruction and support diverse learners, but effective use will require teacher preparation, critical evaluation of tools, and ongoing collaboration among educators, researchers, developers, policymakers, and students with disabilities.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/practice-oriented article rather than an empirical evaluation. It does not report a study design, comparison group, sample, or measured outcomes for Khanmigo or any other intervention.
impact_tier_rationale: No direct impact on K-12 science outcomes is measured. The paper is a framework and illustrative guidance piece, so there is no evidentiary basis to assign a positive impact tier.

interventions.use_case: Conceptual guidance on remixing AI tools into special education practice; includes examples of using Khanmigo for adjusting K-12 content reading level/comprehension, but does not directly evaluate Khanmigo or any other tool.
